notes: Drain graph inferred from roads and terrain, not a municipal SWD model (CLAUDE.md 10.1 step 7); every pipe carries a learned blockage.

Street ensemble: 50 members over 20 Sky rain members through the reduced-order emulator (held-out RMSE 5.7 cm, CSI 0.09 at 30 cm on Twin runs it never saw), each member at its own draw of the pipe blockage from Pulse's posterior and of the emulator's storage coefficient.

Every Sky member is used as often as the count allows rather than resampled with replacement: resampling 50 from 20 moved the reported band by 29.4 % between seeds on the 2 July 08:40 cycle, which is the generator's choice and not the forecast's.

The members differ only in the amplitude of the AOI-mean rain, because that is the only per-member rain a cycle keeps, so the spread is amplitude-driven and carries none of the ensemble's disagreement about where the cell sits.

10 of the 20 Sky members carry 3 ensemble members each and 10 carry 2, because 50 is not a multiple of 20; the weather is therefore weighted 0.060 against 0.040. Measured on the 2 July 08:40 cycle that unbalanced allocation reads a 2.0 % wider band than a balanced 20 x 3, so part of the width is the allocation. Build 60 members for an ensemble with no such artefact in it.
5,543 of 21,296 segments have no pipe in the inferred drain graph to inherit a blockage from and ran at a flat 0.2; that is a substitution, not something Pulse measured.

Ensemble band (mean p90 - p10 of peak depth over 1,491 wet segments): 1.90 cm from all 50 members, 0.59 cm from the 20 Sky rain members alone and 1.50 cm from the parameter draws alone. The blockage draw is the smallest axis: switching it off changes the band by +0.09 cm, which is inside this ensemble's own sampling noise, so the width on screen is the weather's and the emulator's own storage coefficient (log-space MC noise 0.25) and not Pulse's.
The blockage draws came from this cycle's Pulse posterior.
The depth on screen is the Twin's, not the emulator's: Flash supplies the spread around it and never the level (ADR-0025).
Rain ensemble kept as rain/cube.zarr (20 members x 36 steps at 500 m) and rain/quantiles.zarr, so this cycle can be re-ensembled offline without re-running Sky (CLAUDE.md 10.3).
Spatial confounder test: 0 of 13 traffic anomalies rejected as network-wide congestion; the test drops an anomaly whose neighbours within 500 m are all equally slow.
Largest model-observation disagreement: 322 cm at Nathani Road - 20 cm observed against 342 cm from the capacity_deficit operator before the update.
13 observations moved 157 pipes; the update is ES-MDA with perturbed observations (4 passes, 50 members, moment-matched prior draw); the observation operator is capacity_deficit.
NWP blend disabled: no NWP field in P0 (CLAUDE.md 11.1, Appendix A).
Z-R fitted this cycle: a=127, b=1.69 from 20 pairs.
Gauge merge: bias 0.96 over 10 gauges, inverse-distance residuals, gauges honoured to 0.0 %.
Tide series is illustrative, not a published tide table (rule 7).

Tide stage converted from chart datum (assumed: the 4.92 m civic statement does not name its datum; taken as the Apollo Bandar chart datum PSMSL documents) to the DEM's frame by subtracting mean sea level at 2.70 m above chart datum (range 2.66-2.73 m; https://psmsl.org/data/obtaining/stations/43.php, https://psmsl.org/data/obtaining/rlr.annual.data/43.rlrdata). Not quantified: the separation between the EGM2008 geoid, the DEM's datum, and local mean sea level at Mumbai. The conversion puts the stage at mean sea level and treats that as the DEM's frame, so any geoid-to-sea-level offset stays in the tidal boundary as an unmeasured bias, as does any revision of the chart datum since PSMSL's note.
